title: What is Auto Loader (`cloudFiles`) — a Databricks streaming source that incrementally and efficiently processes new files as they arrive in cloud storage, using file notification or directory listing with checkpointing for exactly-once processing?

s1_definition.profdef: Auto Loader is a Databricks Structured Streaming source, invoked with the `cloudFiles` format, that incrementally ingests new files as they land in cloud object storage, processing each file exactly once. It discovers new files either by directory listing or by subscribing to cloud file-notification events, tracks which files it has already processed in a checkpoint, and so avoids both reprocessing old files and missing new ones, even across restarts and at a scale of millions of files.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine the National Bank of India has a mail slot where branches continuously drop new trade statements as files throughout the day. A naive approach is to re-read the entire mail room every time you want the latest statements, which gets slower and slower as the pile grows and risks processing the same statement twice. Auto Loader is like a diligent mail clerk who keeps a precise logbook of exactly which envelopes have already been opened, so each time he only picks up the envelopes that arrived since last time, opens each exactly once, and never loses his place even if he goes home and comes back the next morning. He can either walk the room to see what is new, or, better, get a buzzer every time a new envelope drops so he does not have to keep walking the whole room.
s1_definition.oneliner: Auto Loader incrementally ingests only the new files arriving in cloud storage, exactly once, using checkpointing plus directory listing or file notifications, so it scales to millions of files without reprocessing.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Auto Loader is a Databricks Structured Streaming source, invoked with the `cloudFiles` format, that incrementally ingests new files as they land in cloud object storage, processing each file exactly once. It discovers new files either by directory listing or by subscribing to cloud file-notification events, tracks which files it has already processed in a checkpoint, and so avoids both reprocessing old files and missing new ones, even across restarts and at a scale of millions of files.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Imagine the National Bank of India has a mail slot where branches continuously drop new trade statements as files throughout the day. A naive approach is to re-read the entire mail room every time you want the latest statements, which gets slower and slower as the pile grows and risks processing the same statement twice. Auto Loader is like a diligent mail clerk who keeps a precise logbook of exactly which envelopes have already been opened, so each time he only picks up the envelopes that arrived since last time, opens each exactly once, and never loses his place even if he goes home and comes back the next morning. He can either walk the room to see what is new, or, better, get a buzzer every time a new envelope drops so he does not have to keep walking the whole room.

**One line to remember:** Auto Loader incrementally ingests only the new files arriving in cloud storage, exactly once, using checkpointing plus directory listing or file notifications, so it scales to millions of files without reprocessing.

sections.s2_technical:
A common data engineering task is to ingest files that keep arriving in a cloud storage folder, such as an hourly drop of trade CSVs. The naive batch approach reads the whole folder each run and then tries to figure out what is new, which is slow, error-prone, and gets worse as the folder grows to millions of files because just listing them becomes expensive. Auto Loader is purpose-built for this. You read with the `cloudFiles` format inside a streaming query, for example `spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles").option("cloudFiles.format", "csv").load(path)`, and it incrementally picks up only files that are new since the last processed point. It records the set of processed files in the streaming checkpoint, so on restart it resumes exactly where it left off, which gives exactly-once ingestion semantics: no file is processed twice and none is skipped.

Auto Loader has two file-discovery modes. In directory listing mode it lists the storage path and compares against its checkpoint to find new files; this needs no extra setup and works everywhere but gets costly at very large file counts because listing is expensive on object stores. In file notification mode it sets up cloud-native notifications, using the cloud's event service such as an AWS SNS and SQS queue or an Azure Event Grid and queue, so the storage service pushes a message whenever a new file arrives and Auto Loader consumes those messages instead of repeatedly listing the directory. Notification mode scales to extremely high file volumes because it does not pay the listing cost, at the price of some cloud infrastructure that Auto Loader can provision automatically. You switch with `cloudFiles.useNotifications`, and Auto Loader can even start in listing mode and upgrade to notifications.

Auto Loader also handles schema management, which is a big practical help. It can infer the schema from the incoming files and persist it in a schema location, and it supports schema evolution: when new columns appear, it can automatically add them according to a configured mode, and it can rescue unexpected data into a rescued-data column rather than failing. A senior-level nuance is that Auto Loader is the recommended ingestion source precisely because it combines incremental processing, exactly-once guarantees through checkpointing, scalable discovery through notifications, and schema evolution in one source, replacing fragile custom bookkeeping. Another nuance is that it pairs naturally with the medallion architecture, landing raw files into a bronze Delta table, and with Delta Live Tables for declarative pipelines. The main operational cautions are that the checkpoint and schema location must be preserved for the exactly-once guarantee and schema continuity to hold, that notification mode needs the right cloud permissions, and that in listing mode on huge directories you should still organize files sensibly to keep listing efficient. The practical rule at a bank is to use Auto Loader rather than hand-rolled file tracking for any continuously arriving file feed, because getting exactly-once file ingestion right by hand is hard and Auto Loader does it reliably.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At the National Bank of India, branches continuously drop trade statement files into a cloud storage landing folder throughout the day. The first pipeline re-read the entire folder every hour and tried to diff against what it had seen, but as the folder grew to millions of files the listing alone took longer and longer, and a bug occasionally caused the same file to be processed twice, double-counting trades. This is exactly the problem Auto Loader solves: incremental, exactly-once ingestion of only the new files, with discovery that scales.

This is exactly how Auto Loader works. It keeps a checkpoint of processed files so it only picks up new arrivals, processes each exactly once across restarts, and in notification mode avoids the expensive full listing by consuming file-arrival events.

Problem 2 — Upstream occasionally adds a new column to the trade files, like a new fee field, and the rigid pipeline failed whenever the schema changed. Auto Loader's schema inference and evolution can absorb the new column and rescue unexpected data instead of crashing. This is the schema-evolution capability.

Because we cannot run a real cloud and Databricks, this runnable demo models Auto Loader's core behavior on the local file system. A `CloudStorage` lets files be dropped over time and supports both a listing query and a notification queue. An `AutoLoader` reads new files only, using a checkpoint of processed file names, supports listing versus notification discovery, and handles schema evolution by adding new columns and rescuing extras. A `BronzeTable` receives the ingested rows. The demo drops files in waves, runs Auto Loader repeatedly to show only new files processed and exactly-once behavior across a restart, switches to notification mode, and ingests a file with a new column to show schema evolution.

Configuration file:

```yaml
# application.yml
cloudFiles:
  format: csv
  useNotifications: false        # start with listing; switch to true for scale
  schemaLocation: /chk/trades_schema
  schemaEvolutionMode: addNewColumns
  checkpointLocation: /chk/trades
```

sections.s5_journey:
Input data: trade statement files arriving in waves in cloud storage, starting in listing mode with an empty checkpoint and bronze table.

Step 1: In wave one, two files arrive at nine and ten o'clock. The trigger runs in listing mode, lists all files, sees neither is in the checkpoint, so it ingests both, appends their rows to the bronze table, and marks both as processed in the checkpoint.

Step 2: In wave two, a third file arrives at eleven. The trigger lists all three files, but the first two are already in the checkpoint so they are skipped, and only the new eleven o'clock file is ingested. This is the incremental behavior: old files are never reprocessed.

Step 3: A restart is simulated by triggering again with the same checkpoint and no new files. The trigger lists the three files, finds all three in the checkpoint, and processes nothing new, which demonstrates exactly-once semantics surviving a restart.

Step 4: The loader switches to notification mode. From now on it consumes file-arrival events from the queue instead of listing the whole directory, which is how it scales to millions of files without the listing cost.

Step 5: In wave three, a file arrives with a fourth value, a fee column that the schema did not have. The trigger drains the notification, processes the file, detects the extra column, evolves the bronze schema by adding the fee column, and appends the row rather than failing.

Step 6: The final log shows the bronze table now has the evolved set of columns including fee and the total row count across all ingested files, each file having been processed exactly once.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Auto Loader is a Databricks Structured Streaming source, used with the cloudFiles format, that incrementally ingests new files as they land in cloud object storage and processes each file exactly once. The problem it solves is that the naive approach of re-reading a whole folder every run and diffing to find new files is slow, error-prone, and gets worse as the folder grows to millions of files because listing alone becomes expensive, and it risks processing the same file twice. Auto Loader keeps the set of already-processed files in the streaming checkpoint, so each trigger picks up only the new arrivals, and on restart it resumes exactly where it left off, which gives exactly-once ingestion with no file processed twice and none skipped.

It discovers new files in one of two modes. Directory listing mode lists the path and compares against the checkpoint, which needs no setup but costs more as file counts grow. File notification mode subscribes to the cloud's native file-arrival events through a queue, so the storage pushes a message for each new file and Auto Loader consumes those instead of listing, which scales to very high file volumes, and it can even provision that notification infrastructure automatically. On top of discovery, Auto Loader handles schema management: it can infer and persist the schema in a schema location and evolve it when new columns appear, rescuing unexpected data into a rescued-data column rather than failing. That combination of incremental processing, exactly-once via checkpointing, scalable notification-based discovery, and schema evolution is why it is the recommended ingestion source, replacing fragile hand-rolled file tracking, and it pairs naturally with the bronze-silver-gold medallion architecture and Delta Live Tables.

At the National Bank of India this fixed a real pipeline. Branches continuously dropped trade statement files into a landing folder, and our original hourly pipeline re-read the whole folder and diffed it, which got slower as the folder reached millions of files and occasionally double-counted trades when a file was processed twice. We switched to Auto Loader, which only picked up new files, processed each exactly once across restarts thanks to the checkpoint, and once we moved it to notification mode it stopped paying the listing cost and scaled comfortably. When upstream added a new fee column to the files, Auto Loader's schema evolution absorbed it instead of crashing the job. The operational discipline I stress is to preserve the checkpoint and schema location because the exactly-once guarantee and schema continuity depend on them, and to grant the cloud permissions notification mode needs. The rule I follow is to never hand-roll file tracking for a continuously arriving feed, because getting exactly-once file ingestion right by hand is hard and Auto Loader does it reliably.
